Management Plan
- Localized reaction to insect sting suspected; no current features of anaphylaxis on video assessment.
- OTC antihistamines advised: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet up to six times daily, or a once-daily antihistamine per patient preference.
- Education on red flags and when to seek urgent care: lip/tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, rapidly progressing symptoms—attend Emergency Department immediately.
- Monitor sting site; if redness spreads, area becomes hot/tender, or signs of local infection develop, seek care to consider antibiotics.
- Allergy testing not indicated now; consider if recurrent reactions or unexplained rashes occur.
- Patient provided informational link on anaphylaxis; advised low threshold to recontact if worried.
